## Functional summary

The sequence is **NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 (ND1; also called MT-ND1)**, a core membrane subunit of **mitochondrial respiratory-chain Complex I**.

The identification is highly confident: the sequence exactly matches a reviewed UniProt ND1 reference (**O78696**, *Lemur catta*) over its full length, with 100% identity and coverage. It also contains the characteristic **NADHdh Pfam domain, PF00146**, spanning approximately residues 5–304.

### Key features

| Feature | Result |
|---|---|
| Length | 318 amino acids |
| Approximate molecular mass | 35.8 kDa |
| Theoretical pI | 7.73 |
| GRAVY hydrophobicity score | 0.774 |
| Predicted topology | Strongly hydrophobic, multi-pass membrane protein |
| Localization | Mitochondrial inner membrane |
| Complex association | Core membrane arm of respiratory Complex I |
| Domain | NADHdh, PF00146 |
| Identification confidence | Very high; exact full-length reference match |

### Biological role

ND1 forms part of the membrane arm of **NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase, or Complex I**. Complex I transfers electrons from NADH toward ubiquinone and couples this process to proton translocation across the inner mitochondrial membrane. ND1 is primarily a membrane-embedded structural and functional component of the complex and is important for complex I assembly and catalytic activity.

The sequence itself is dominated by long hydrophobic stretches with very few charged residues, consistent with multiple membrane-spanning helices. It is therefore not expected to function as a soluble NADH-binding enzyme independently; its activity depends on its incorporation into the full Complex I assembly.

**Conclusion:** this is a mitochondrial Complex I ND1 subunit, most likely encoded by mitochondrial DNA in the source organism. The functional assignment is supported by exact sequence identity, strong family-domain evidence, and concordant reviewed annotations.
